# **CFTC and ETF Report** _A weekly update of futures and exchange traded fund activity._ - All of the precious metal prices (including rhodium) climbed over the end of January. For gold and platinum, this just seemed to be part of the month-long rush higher which investors had initiated. The move was aided by a weak Dollar but this now appears to be firming instead, placing prices under some pressure. Palladium toyed with the $700 level before eventually moving above in early February (and falling back since). Silver was relatively quiet by its own standards. Good US employment figures dented the (previously excessive) hopes of QE3 being launched to place the metal complex under pressure. Supply side disruption in South Africa should provide a degree of support to platinum and palladium prices. - Futures exchange investors were friendly towards all of the precious metals in the final week of January. Gold and silver saw good buying interest. Platinum and palladium also saw substantial fresh long positions established. However, of these two metals, platinum appears more crowded with positioning closer to its 2011 peak than palladium. • All four of the major metals saw net inflows into their ETFs in the week to the 3rd of February. Silver and gold saw some buying interest but this was rather restrained. Platinum investors were more positive but the stand-out performer was palladium where the move through $700 seems to have attracted buying interest. In a market which most people believe should be in deficit this year, buying of 100,000 ounces of ETF metal in only two weeks is a powerful signal. Elsewhere, the rhodium ETF recorded a net inflow of 3,500 ounces, its largest weekly change since its launch as rhodium prices slowly firmed. ##### **David Jollie** **david.jollie@mitprecious.com Tel: +44 20 7489 6767** **06 February 2012** ##### **New York:** 200 Park Avenue, New York, NY 10166 0130 Tel: +1 212 878 4122 ##### **London:** 4th Floor, St Martins Court, 10 Paternoster Row, London EC4M 7BB Tel: +44 20 7489 6767 ##### **Hong Kong:** Suite 1306, Two Exchange Square, 8 Connaught Place, Central, Hong Kong Tel: +852 2899 2026 ##### **Tokyo:** 2-1 Ohtemachi 1-Chome, Chiyoda-Ku, Tokyo 100 Tel: +81 33 285 3407 ##### **Singapore:** 80 Robinson Road, #15-02, Singapore, 068898 Tel: +65 6372 8050 **Mitsui Global Precious Metals | CFTC and ETF Weekly Report** **06 February 2012** ### **Gold CFTC data to 31 January 2012; ETF data to 3 February 2012.** #### **Exchange (COMEX and TOCOM) and ETF Gold Investment (oz)** ||**COMEX**

While this movement has been positive, gold has still not challenged its highs of just under $1,800 made in November, which should be the first major challenge on its way towards the all-time nominal highs of August 2011. The Dollar weakened throughout the second half of the month, driven partly by the FOMC’s comments on the 25th that US interest rates would remain at a low level until late-2014. Gold leapt from $1,650 to $1,710 that day and then climbed in almost a straight line to touch $1,760 on the 3rd of February. However, better-than-expected US non-farm payroll data placed gold under pressure late on the 3rd and it has since fallen back towards $1,720. Although we are positive over the outlook for the gold price, with the Euro looking a little weaker the next challenge to the gold price is likely to come from the foreign exchange markets. - Net long speculative positions on COMEX climbed by 3.5 million ounces to 22.8 million ounces in the final week of January as long interest climbed sharply and any short positions were punished by the constantly-rising price. We believe the sharp decline in the price on Friday and today is likely to have driven some long liquidation since the CFTC data was released. - Gold ETF positions increased for the fourth successive week, rising a further 300,000 ounces last week to 70.2 million ounces (a near record level) at the end of January. Most of the funds which we monitor recorded net inflows of metal as the economic environment remains positive for gold. We note, however, that inflows were not overly large given the strength of the gold price. #### **Gold Exchange Investment, Jan 10 — Jan 12** 40 2,000 Gold price, $/oz

- Following its remarkably bullish start to the year, the end of January was a more neutral period for the silver price. Having ripped higher following the FOMC’s comments that US interest rates were likely to remain at low levels until late-2014, silver burst through the $33 level on the 26th and continued to climb to almost $34 on the 30th of January. After a brief period of consolidation, it firmed to $34.36 per ounce on the 2nd and 3rd of February. When gold was caught up in strong US employment figures and fell back, silver was swept lower too, dropping to support at $33.50 at the end of the 3rd and falling below to roughly $33.20 in morning trading in London on the 6th. - Net long speculative silver positions on COMEX grew by 18.3 million ounces, their fifth consecutive weekly increase, something that has been a large driving force for the higher silver price. Fresh new lon

g positions were opened, suggesting that the risk-reward balance in silver is still attractive to some investors. Short covering provided a boost to the price too. Total net exposure is now 161 million ounces, 70 million ounces higher than at the start of the year. Although this is lower than its peak levels last year, higher margins should make further gains more difficult to achieve than last year. - Silver ETF positions grew by 3.8 million ounces in the week to the 3rd of February. They now stand at 456 million ounces, essentially unchanged from where they were at the start of the year. Inflows of metal into the largest fund, iShares were a surprising positive: the last time this fund took in net new metal was in the week to the 9th of December. 3 **Mitsui Global Precious Metals | CFTC and ETF Weekly Report** **06 February 2012** ### **Platinum CFTC data to 31 January 2012; ETF data to 3 February 2012.** ## **Exchange (Nymex and TOCOM) and ETF Platinum Investment (oz)** ||**Nymex**

||||||| |**Date**|**ZKB**|**ETFS (UK)**|**ETFS (US)**|**Julius Baer**|**Other**|**Total**|| |**27-Jan-12**|368,856|380,471|476,006|104,140|107,642|**1,437,115**|| |**03-Feb-12**|368,856|384,550|480,559|106,640|106,971|**1,447,576**|| |**Change**|**0**|**4,079**|**4,553**|**2,500**|**-671**|**10,461**|| - Platinum’s price performance was a little more measured than that of gold in late January and early February. Nonetheless, the move from $1,400 at the start of the year to highs of $1,635 on the 3rd of February can hardly be considered moderate or sustainable. When gold leapt $60 higher on the 25th over fears/hopes that US interest rates would remain at low levels for a very extended period, platinum was slower in moving but still gained $75 over two days in reaching $1,620. It did press higher, closing in on $1,630 on the last day of January before a stronger Dollar and a touch of optimism over the Greek negotiations sent the price plunging to $1,685. The recovery to $1,635 on the 3rd despite a strengthening Dollar was aided by news stories of some supply side disruption in South Africa. Further Dollar weakness and a falling gold price has since sent platinum back down to $1,610. - Although TOCOM investors shortened their exposure to platinum in the last week of January, NYMEX investors behaved differently with net long speculative positions climbing strongly. They rose by 190,000 ounces to 1.47 million ounces. Although this

is still roughly 300,000 ounces short of the highest positioning seen last year, the market feels a little over-extended. The pullbacks on the 31st of January and the 6th of February illustrate the challenges this speculative length can bring. - Platinum ETF holdings have now increased for five consecutive weeks, adding a total 46,000 ounces to stand at a current 1.448 million ounces. Buying interest was widespread last week with net inflows into both European and North American funds. Interestingly, the outflows from the Source fund continued. This held almost 40,000 ounces in August last year but its holdings have now declined to below 5,000 ounces. #### **Platinum Exchange Investment Jan 10 — Jan 12** 2,500 2,000

||||||| |**Date**|**ZKB**|**ETFS (UK)**|**ETFS (US)**|**Julius Baer**|**Other**|**Total**|| |**27-Jan-12**|402,836|459,145|636,606|123,243|149,189|**1,771,019**|| |**03-Feb-12**|402,386|470,363|665,690|123,243|164,189|**1,825,871**|| |**Change**|**-450**|**11,218**|**29,084**|**0**|**15,000**|**54,852**|| - Palladium followed a slightly different price trajectory to the other precious metals in late January. On the 25th, the FOMC’s doveish comments depressed the Dollar and sent gold soaring by $60. Palladium moved a similar distance in percentage terms, firming from $675 to $695 that day. The move higher was halted, though by resistance at the $70 level on the 26th. Palladium backtracked to wards $680 at the start of the following week but with inv

estors now more bullish and ETF buying returning, there was upwards pressure. Short-lived challenges to the $700 level were made on the 31st of January and 1st of February but both failed. On the 2nd, however, all of the metals moved higher in afternoon trading and palladium was finally catapulted through the resistance to a high of $715. With gold falling back, palladium has since weakened. It bounced off support at $700 early on the 6th of February but has since fallen below that level to $695. - Net long speculative positions in palladium on NYMEX increased by another 133,000 ounces in the final week of January as fresh long positions were added. They climbed to 956,000 ounces, over double their level of only a few weeks earlier and their longest since September. Although the increase in speculative interest is substantial, palladium currently feels less crowded than platinum. - ETF investors purchased a net 55,000 ounces in the week to the 3rd of February, with palladium holdings rising to 1.83 million ounces. Most of the funds we monitor recorded net buying interest and, after four weeks of buying, investor sentiment seems to have improved. At the time of writing, palladium is back below $700, however, and we feel that it needs to remain above that level to generate additional buying. #### **Palladium Exchange Investment, Jan 10 — Jan 12** 2,000 1,000
